Figure_6_three_seed_AP: Figure 6. Training-seed variation of the three domain-configured DENT-STRIDE models. Circles show the actual AP obtained with seeds 0, 1, and 2; diamonds and error bars show the mean and sample standard deviation. (A) DENTEX2023 with anatomical scoring. (B) Mobile. (C) DSLR. Each panel has an independent AP axis to display within-cohort variation. All estimates use validation-selected checkpoints on the respective fixed image partitions; the error bars are not patient-level confidence intervals.
Figure_7_DSLR_accuracy_size: Optional DSLR size comparison. (A) Framework-level comparison, including RT-DETR-L. (B) Enlarged view of the smaller models. DENT-STRIDE-DSLR, Official DEIM-s, and RT-DETRv2-S are plotted as three-seed means with sample-standard-deviation error bars; open circles denote single-seed conventional-detector results without a dispersion estimate. DENT-STRIDE-DSLR uses 11.154 M parameters and achieves 72.293 ± 0.651 AP. The detector systems retain their framework-specific training and pretraining settings. No Pareto-frontier connection is imposed, and the figure does not establish a size–accuracy advantage over Official DEIM-s.
Figure_7_Mobile_framework_AP: Figure 7. Framework-level detection AP on Mobile images. DENT-STRIDE-Mobile, Official DEIM-s, and RT-DETRv2-S are shown as three-seed means with sample-standard-deviation error bars; open circles indicate single-seed detector results. All external comparators are retained, including RT-DETR-L. DENT-STRIDE-Mobile achieves the highest numerical mean AP among the displayed detector systems (55.219 ± 0.327). The models retain framework-specific resolution, pretraining, optimization, and post-processing, so the plot describes complete detector systems rather than an isolated module effect or statistical superiority.
Figure_9_Pano_prior_comparison: Figure 9. Anatomical scoring on the same three DENTEX2023 checkpoints. None, center-only, shape-only, and combined center–shape settings are evaluated from candidates before top-k selection. Circles show individual-seed results and diamonds show mean ± sample standard deviation. (A) COCO AP. (B) AR100. Center scoring improves mean AP by 0.494 points relative to no prior; combined scoring improves AP by 0.484 points and gives the highest mean AR100. The same checkpoint is retained across the four scoring settings within each seed; these comparisons measure inference corrections rather than training effects.
Figure_11_HOOA_Factor_learning_effects: Figure 11. Learning-effect ablations on Mobile images with seed 0. Bars show AP differences from the intact setting within each group, using separately trained models. (A) Removing the HOOA high-pass branch, second-order interaction, or both reduces AP by 0.399, 0.967, or 1.349 points relative to the full-module reference (54.910 AP). (B) Removing quadrant, position, or dentition supervision reduces AP by 0.654, 1.274, or 0.244 points relative to the all-factor reference (55.537 AP). Training and inference factor-score fusion are disabled in all supervision comparisons. No across-seed uncertainty is assigned to these single-seed ablations.
Figure_S6_component_sensitivity: Figure S6. Component and training-setting sensitivity on seed 0. Signed AP differences are relative to the stated group reference, not to a universal baseline. (A–C, E) Reference: the Mobile configuration with both CMFA gates, four prototypes at temperature 0.20, and both background losses (54.910 AP). (D) Reference: DSLR CMFA with ordinary AdamW (72.892 AP), with its standard weight decay unchanged across the additional operations. (F) Reference: Mobile with factor fusion disabled during training and inference (55.537 AP). All learning changes use separately trained models; within each training-fusion state, inference on/off reuses the same weights. Every tested setting is retained, including settings that exceed the intact configuration. These single-seed comparisons have no repeated-seed error bars.
Figure_S12_prior_paired_AP_intervals: Figure S12. Paired AP effects of DENTEX2023 anatomical scoring relative to no prior, using the same checkpoint within each seed. Grey circles show the three actual paired differences; diamonds show their mean and horizontal bars show Student-t 95% confidence intervals for the three-seed mean (df=2). Center-only, shape-only, and joint scoring are all retained. The checkpoint selection used the configured prior, and the intervals describe seed variation on the same validation split; they are not patient-level sampling intervals or independent-test evidence.
Figure_S5_learning_curves: Figure S5. Validation-AP learning curves of the final domain-configured models over 160 epochs. (A) DENTEX2023. (B) Mobile. (C) DSLR. Thin grey lines show the actual epoch-wise results of seeds 0, 1, and 2, distinguished by solid, dashed, and dotted line styles. The blue line and shaded band show the epoch-wise mean and sample standard deviation across the three seeds, without smoothing. The panels include all 160 recorded epochs from the current completed runs. These epoch-wise averages differ from the mean of each seed’s individually selected best checkpoint reported in Table 3.
